title: Choose the visual world for Ares Sales
question: The roll assigned Department Signage. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Department Signage
options.lineage: hospital wayfinding: colour-banded department blades, arrows, pictogram plates
options.thesis: Every visit is filed the way a hospital is navigated: a colour-coded blade tells you the department before you read the name.
options.viewport: Charcoal sign-blade rail on the left with the gold Ares mark at top and nav items set as blades with arrows; the work area on warm signage-white: filters across the top, then the directory board of visits, each row led by a solid colour block naming the customer type (PATH, HOSP, CLIN) in white, then customer name large, contact, purpose, instrument count, and date in tabular figures; the primary Log a visit action sits top right in gold. Selecting a row slides a detail blade in from the right with its photos on pictogram-style plates.
options.risk: If the colour blocks are thinned to borders or the type is set small, it collapses into an ordinary admin table.

raised.raise: Fixed columns: a changed status restyles the row, never the grid.
One colour owns every live state: gold, and nothing else is gold.
Every instrument photo sits in one fixed frame on a shared baseline, so a customer's units compare at a glance.
The photo gallery repacks in whole cells; nothing is ever half shown.
One timing law: every transition shares one duration and one curve.

options.label: Cap-Colour Rack
options.lineage: the blood-tube cap colour code every lab reads daily: gold SST, lavender EDTA, blue citrate, green heparin, red plain
options.thesis: Status is a cap colour, and the gold SST cap is Ares: the whole record system reads at the speed a phlebotomist reads a rack.
options.viewport: Light bench-white ground with a pale rack-grey top bar carrying the Ares mark and the cap legend as the filter row; the visit list below with a glossy round cap chip leading each row (gold = Ares installed, blue = competitor, lavender = demo, red = needs service), customer, contact, purpose, and date; the gallery panel on the right holds photos in a 5-across rack grid, each with its cap on top and a thermal-label tag beneath; Log a visit in gold top right.
options.risk: The most familiar destination for this audience: a coloured status chip is also what every CRM ships.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.lineage: the segmented boarding pass and the live gate board
options.thesis: A visit is a pass with labelled segments and tabular figures; the records board ranks visits by date and holds a changed row in gold until it is seen.
options.viewport: Neutral panel ground; the records board fills the centre as a fixed-column ranking by visit date; the selected visit opens on the right as a segmented pass: customer, date, contact, purpose, outcome, each a labelled segment, instrument serials in a monospaced block; edited or new rows flash gold and hold it.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: labelled segments and tabular figures make records unmistakable, and held change state is exactly what a manager scanning the board needs; loses on audience identification, since lab people have their own artifacts and this reads as travel.
options.risk: Reads as an airline app when the pass segments get decorative.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Visits as departures: rows ranked by time, letters flipping as records change.
options.viewport: A black ranked board of visits with per-character flips.
options.case: Loses both axes: lab reps do not see themselves in a rail concourse, and a flipping cascade is noise on a form-heavy working screen.
options.kept: Fixed columns: state restyles the row, never the grid.
options.risk: Reads as a station, not a sales tool.

options.label: Metro Typographic Tiles
options.lineage: flat tiles, giant lowercase, chrome deleted
options.thesis: Visits and photos as flat live tiles; type is the interface.
options.viewport: A black panorama of tiles with cropped giant headlines.
options.case: Loses both axes: a 2012 phone OS is nobody's world in a pathology lab, and deleting chrome deletes the affordances a visit form needs.
options.kept: One colour owns every live state.
options.risk: Reads as a dated phone OS.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: one plant through five fixed-scale plates
options.thesis: A customer's instruments as plates on one baseline, compared over visits.
options.viewport: Five cream plates on a shared baseline.
options.case: Loses both axes: cream folio and engraved italics belong to a botanist, and the plate sequence serves a gallery but not a visit form or a filterable board.
options.kept: Fixed-frame photo registration on a shared baseline.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Every instrument photo as a stamp in a numbered hall grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: a fan-convention catalogue is foreign to this audience, and stamp-sized thumbs hide the serial plates the record depends on.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.lineage: flat colour lobes with a coastline between them
options.thesis: Customers as coloured lobes on a cream map.
options.viewport: One swelling green lobe with capsule controls.
options.case: Loses both axes: a leisure map does not read as a sales record, and letting a lobe drive layout is exactly what an Operate surface forbids.
options.kept: One timing law for every transition.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A CRM-style records app: white ground, dark sidebar, cards and a data table, gold as the accent.
canonCard.viewport: Dark sidebar, KPI cards across the top, a visits table below, a Log a visit button in gold.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any other field-sales tool by design.
